clue.text: This could be statement Matthew's found at the start of this collection

definitions.text: Matthew's found at the start of this collection

indicators.note: a reverse clue: the answer read as an instruction says to make the following word anew, so its letters get rearranged

blocks.note: the answer itself opens with the instruction 'new', the signal to rearrange what follows
rearranging these nine letters gives a word meaning a will or witness

explanation.surface: A note that Matthew's Gospel opens some anthology.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: NEW TESTAMENT, read cryptically as 'new testament', is an instruction to rearrange TESTAMENT, and the result is 'statement'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gospel of Matthew is the first book of the Christian scriptures' second part, the New Testament.

clue.text: Most organised revision, finally, before each exam

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word just before it, keeping only its closing letter

blocks.note: the last letter of revision
EA is the standard abbreviation for each
an exam is a test

explanation.surface: A student doing the tidiest revision just before every exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatest is the superlative of neat, meaning tidy or well organised.

clue.text: Newspaper cutting was showing bears

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into the middle of another word, so this piece sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A press clipping that showed some bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like the animals in the cutting, but is a verb meaning carries.
explanation.definitionFit: To waft is to carry something gently through the air, so wafts means bears along.

clue.text: Old little room on hospital department is fantastic

blocks.note: ex- means former or old
a cell is a small room
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: An old cramped room in a hospital ward gets praised as fantastic.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' means placed above, so the first pieces sit on top of ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellent and fantastic are both informal terms of strong approval, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Grasp tiny branch

blocks.note: first meaning: to understand, informally
second meaning: a slender shoot of a tree

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests clutching a small stick; 'grasp' is really understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal British slang for suddenly understanding, and also a small shoot off a branch.

clue.text: One retained by church?

indicators.note: something retained by another thing is held within it

blocks.note: a minster is a large church, such as York Minster
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A clergyman kept on the books of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a cleric employed by a church, and also tells you to put 'one' inside a big church.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman serving a congregation is employed and kept in post by that church, and the question mark marks the whole-clue reading.

clue.text: Some begin at a lovely old part of South Africa

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across letters 5-9 of 'begin at a lovely'

explanation.surface: Someone starting a description of a lovely former province.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal was a province of South Africa until 1994, now KwaZulu-Natal.

clue.text: I knew rat damaged clothing

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters lose their order

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone suspected a rat had chewed the clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitwear is the general term for knitted garments such as jumpers and cardigans.

clue.text: Grooms might need these black horses?

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
rides are horses one rides, mounts; the question mark flags the loose sense

explanation.surface: Stable grooms might need black horses to look after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grooms' and 'horses' suggest stable hands; the grooms are bridegrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridegroom needs a woman getting married to him, so wedding grooms need these partners.

clue.text: Female wearing fine coat woven for warmth

indicators.note: to wear something is to have it around you, so this letter sits inside the rest
woven threads are interlaced and redirected, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman putting on a good woven coat to keep warm.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of 'fine coat' wear F, which goes in after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth of feeling towards someone is fondness, so warmth serves as a synonym here.

clue.text: Singer from Turkey bored by English National Opera

indicators.note: a thing bored by something has a hole drilled into it and filled, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey
ENO is the English National Opera

explanation.surface: A Turkish singer finding the English National Opera dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bored' looks like weariness, but means drilled into, so one piece goes inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with the highest ordinary adult voice.

clue.text: Small mammals taking off with artist's equipment?

indicators.note: taking something off removes it, so a letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: weasels are small carnivorous mammals
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Weasels running off with a painter's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: W, for 'with', is taken off WEASELS. The question mark marks the definition as one example of an artist's kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters set their canvases on stands, so these stands are part of an artist's equipment.

clue.text: One criticised about ordinary remote

indicators.note: about means going around something, so one word surrounds another

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to slate is to criticise harshly
O is the abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: Someone attacked for being too ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criticised' looks like a verb on the surface; it is the past participle slated, which wraps the ordinary letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote place is far away and cut off, so remote and isolated are synonyms.

clue.text: Pinches gallery's frames silently at first

indicators.note: a frame surrounds a picture, so this word surrounds the letter that follows
at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: the Tate is a London gallery, so gallery's gives Tate's
the first letter of silently

explanation.surface: A gallery quietly stealing pictures and framing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinches' looks like stealing, but means small amounts, as of salt. The Tate is London's national gallery group.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinch of salt is a taste of it, so pinches and tastes both mean small samples.

clue.text: Roughly describes singular vessels

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for singular
ketches are two-masted sailing boats

explanation.surface: A loose account of some unusual ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' looks like an adjective meaning odd, but is the grammar abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To sketch something is to give an outline of it without detail, a rough description.

clue.text: Wobbly knees – was showing frailty

indicators.note: something wobbly is unsteady and will not hold its shape, so these letters move about

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone's wobbly knees revealed how frail they were.
explanation.definitionFit: Frailty is a lack of strength, and the answer names that same lack.

clue.text: After Keir's first upset we longed for expertise

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the name just before it
something upset is knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged
after places what follows behind the initial letter, setting the order of the pieces

blocks.note: the first letter of Keir
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Political supporters, upset by Keir Starmer, wishing for real expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertise is skill and understanding in a field, which is what this word for learned information means.

clue.text: Guess I'm stuck in car?

indicators.note: something stuck in another thing is lodged inside it

blocks.note: an estate is a British car with a long rear load area, a station wagon
taken as written

explanation.surface: A driver stuck in a car can only guess when they'll arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon; the question mark flags it as one kind of car.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to make an approximate judgement, which is what a guess is.

clue.text: Cover that is including small piece of writing

indicators.note: including means holding something within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: to cover the bill is to treat someone
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A note on covering some small written work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' means paying for someone, as in covering the drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written work dealing systematically with a subject.

clue.text: Proposes book containing stories? Just the opposite

indicators.note: containing means holding inside; 'just the opposite' flips which word holds which

blocks.note: tales are stories
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a book of stories, then reverses the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, B would contain TALES; 'just the opposite' means TALES contains B.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage, to table a motion is to put it forward for discussion, to propose it.

clue.text: Male swan spots short snakes

indicators.note: short means cut off before its end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: a cob is a male swan
a rash is an outbreak of spots

explanation.surface: A cock swan notices some small snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' looks like a verb meaning sees, but is the noun: RASH, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobras are venomous hooded snakes of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Nurses unfortunately stress about heart of patient

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are knocked out of order
the heart is the middle, so only the centre letter of the next word is kept
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the kept letter

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
the middle letter of patient

explanation.surface: Nurses, sadly, fret over a patient's heart condition.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a senior nurse is called Sister, so 'Nurses' fairly defines the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: In UK hospitals a senior nurse in charge of a ward holds the title Sister.

clue.text: Something created by tennis player perhaps supports leg

definitions.text: Something created by tennis player perhaps

blocks.note: to back someone is to support them
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: A tennis player's injury, perhaps, needs support for the leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pins' is informal British for legs, so one leg is a pin.
explanation.definitionFit: Backspin is the backward rotation a player puts on a ball by slicing under it, as tennis players do.

clue.text: Kind, upright member by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is judged by how it is spoken, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: in joinery, a stile is an upright member of a door or window frame

explanation.surface: A friendly, honourable member of some club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' and 'upright member' read as praise for a decent person; both are carpentry and type senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A style is a type or sort of something, so kind serves as its synonym.

clue.text: Walks around large homes

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: paces are walking steps; to pace is to walk
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone strolls past some big houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, someone's place is their home, as in 'come back to my place'.

clue.text: Crew oddly guarding an old boat

indicators.note: oddly keeps the letters in odd-numbered positions of the word
guarding means standing on either side of something to protect it, so it goes inside

blocks.note: the first and third letters of crew
taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A strange crew protecting an ancient vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like 'strangely' but keeps letters one and three of 'Crew'.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light narrow boat paddled by hand.

clue.text: Give up completely? Not completely

indicators.note: not completely means a word falls just short, losing its final letter

blocks.note: quite can mean completely, as in 'quite right'

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether to abandon a habit entirely, then deciding to cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks whether to give up entirely; the first 'completely' is the word, the second phrase trims it.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit is to stop doing or abandon something, which is what giving up means.

clue.text: Peonies regularly pruned by my adversary

indicators.note: pruning at regular intervals cuts every other letter, leaving the alternate ones

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of peonies
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardening rival cut back my peonies.
explanation.definitionFit: An adversary is an opponent or foe, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Sailor with flipping new uniform before trip, displaying wealth

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the following short pair of letters runs backwards

blocks.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
N is the abbreviation for new
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet
to trip, as in trip the light fantastic, is to dance

explanation.surface: A sailor in a brand-new uniform shows off his wealth before a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British expletive; it reverses N and U. 'Trip' looks like a journey but is a light step.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance is plentiful supply, and so riches or wealth in a loose sense.

clue.text: Craft three lenses, keeping very still

indicators.note: to craft is to shape by hand, so these letters are reworked into a new form
keeping means holding on to something inside

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: An optician grinding three lenses while holding them perfectly still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' sits at the end looking like 'motionless'; it is the adverb meaning 'even so'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, still can mean however or in spite of that, the same sense as this word.
